title: Built a $0.01-per-call crypto sentiment API for AI agents (x402 protocol, real USDC payments on Base)
author: Forge-Alone
selftext: I've been learning about x402 — HTTP 402 "Payment Required" repurposed for AI agents to autonomously pay for API access — and built a small service around it: real-time crypto sentiment scoring from 10 crypto news outlets and the Fear & Greed Index. $0.01 per call, no signup, no API key — the payment itself is the auth. Live on Base mainnet with real settled transactions. [https://crypto-sentiment-x402.onrender.com/sentiment/BTC](https://crypto-sentiment-x402.onrender.com/sentiment/BTC) Curious what people think, both of the API itself and of x402 as a monetization model generally — it's still pretty obscure.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the payment-is-the-auth bit is the interesting part, no signup is genuinely nice for an agent. the sentiment score is where I'd want to see something before paying even a cent a call: does it lead BTC on any horizon, or follow it? every news sentiment feed I've personally looked at was a lagging summary of the move that had already happened. if you've measured lead or lag, put that on the page, it's the whole sell.

replies.author: Forge-Alone
replies.body: Fair question, and the honest answer is I don't know yet. It's VADER scored over published headlines, so my expectation is coincident-to-lagging, same pattern you've seen. I've only been logging daily snapshots for about a month, which is far too few points to say anything either way, so I'm not going to claim a result. Now switching to hourly logging so I can test lead/lag properly, and if it turns out to be useless as a lead signal I'll say so.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: hourly is the right call, a month of daily snapshots is barely 20 points. and when you publish it, put the lag result on the page even if it's ugly. a feed that admits it follows the move by an hour is more useful to an agent than one that claims to lead and can't show it.
